papers.title: A 3D bioprinter platform for mechanistic analysis of tumoroids and chimeric mammary organoids.
papers.abstract: The normal mammary microenvironment can suppress tumorigenesis and redirect cancer cells to adopt a normal mammary epithelial cell fate in vivo. Understanding of this phenomenon offers great promise for novel treatment and detection strategies in cancer, but current model systems make mechanistic insights into the process difficult. We have recently described a low-cost bioprinting platform designed to be accessible for basic cell biology laboratories. Here we report the use of this system for the study of tumorigenesis and microenvironmental redirection of breast cancer cells. We show our bioprinter significantly increases tumoroid formation in 3D collagen gels and allows for precise generation of tumoroid arrays. We also demonstrate that we can mimic published in vivo findings by co-printing cancer cells along with normal mammary epithelial cells to generate chimeric organoids. These chimeric organoids contain cancer cells that take part in normal luminal formation. Furthermore, we show for the first time that cancer cells within chimeric structures have a significant increase in 5-hydroxymethylcytosine levels as compared to bioprinted tumoroids. These results demonstrate the capacity of our 3D bioprinting platform to study tumorigenesis and microenvironmental control of breast cancer and highlight a novel mechanistic insight into the process of microenvironmental control of cancer.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文描述了一个3D生物打印平台用于肿瘤模型，但未涉及任何AI或机器学习方法，与AI驱动生物打印方向无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on a bioprinting platform for tumor biology and does not incorporate AI or machine learning into any stage of the bioprinting workflow.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究肿瘤微环境对癌细胞重编程的现象。
summary_zh.method: 使用低成本3D生物打印平台共打印癌细胞和正常乳腺上皮细胞。
summary_zh.result: 共打印形成嵌合类器官，癌细胞参与正常腺腔形成且5hmC水平升高。
summary_zh.validation: 通过共聚焦显微镜和免疫组化验证细胞结构。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the tumor-suppressive microenvironment that can redirect cancer cell fate using a 3D bioprinting platform.
summary_en.method: Cancer cells and normal mammary epithelial cells were co-printed using a low-cost bioprinter to generate chimeric organoids.
summary_en.result: Co-printed chimeric organoids showed cancer cells participating in normal luminal formation with increased 5-hydroxymethylcytosine levels.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed via confocal microscopy and immunohistochemistry to confirm cell organization and epigenetic changes.
